page.title: Fleet
page.purpose: Answer the operator's first question — which devices do I control, what can each actually do right now, and what is running on them.

priorities.statement: Every controlled device is listed with its probed capability tier, never its assumed one.
priorities.notes: A device kind usually having a capability is not evidence. The list shows what was proven at the last probe.

priorities.statement: An unavailable capability names its missing prerequisite and next action inline.
priorities.notes: 'Unavailable' with no reason forces the operator into the CLI to find out why.

priorities.statement: A device with a live session is visually distinct from an idle one.
priorities.notes: The operator must never have to open a device to discover something is driving it.

states.description: The fleet as the live system reports it.
Inventory is being fetched; no device rows are asserted yet.
Bridge is reachable but no devices are attached. Explains how to attach one.
Devices are listed and at least one capability is unavailable or unsupported. The normal working state, not a degraded one.
The newest capability snapshot is older than the probe interval; shown as stale rather than silently trusted.
The inventory request failed. Devices already known are still listed with their reachability unknown rather than removed.
One or more devices with fresh probed capability tiers and no outstanding gaps.
The specific form of request-error where the reach plane itself is unreachable. Every device reports unreachable carrying that reason rather than vanishing.
At least one device is under a held lease. The lease bar is present and the holding row is distinguished.

elements.name: Live session
elements.description: Global alarm shown whenever any device is under a held lease. Carries holder, elapsed time, and expiry countdown.

elements.name: Kill session
elements.description: Immediate session termination. Lives in the lease bar so its position is identical on every route.

elements.name: Unavailable
elements.description: Fleet-wide count of capabilities that are probed-and-absent. The page's most important negative signal.

elements.name: Fleet summary
elements.description: Counts band: devices, reachable, live sessions, unavailable capabilities, stale probes.

elements.name: Devices
elements.description: One row per device-and-strategy pair, because a device is only meaningful through a strategy.

elements.name: capabilities
elements.description: Ten-cell graphic summary of the probed capability set. Its text alternative states the available, unavailable, and not-probed counts so the distinction survives without color.
Per-device reachability disposition, rendered as a disposition chip.
The missing prerequisite and the next action for an unavailable capability, shown inline rather than behind a drill-in.
When the capability snapshot was taken, and whether it is past the probe interval.
Empty-state instructions for attaching a device through the bridge fleet.
Assertive notice that the reach plane is unreachable, naming bridge as the cause.

claims.statement: When a capability is unavailable, its missing prerequisite and next action are perceivable on this page without opening a detail view.
claims.rationale: Priority 2. An unavailable disposition with no reason forces the operator into the CLI, which defeats the point of the console.

claims.statement: Each device's capability summary is accompanied by the freshness of the probe that produced it.
claims.rationale: Priority 1 and D-002. A capability summary with no probe timestamp is indistinguishable from an assumption.

claims.statement: A fleet whose newest snapshot is past the probe interval is perceivably different from one that is current.
claims.rationale: D-002 forbids silently trusting an old probe; the UI must therefore show the difference rather than rendering both identically.

claims.statement: A capability that has never been probed is presented differently from one that was probed and found absent.
claims.rationale: The core honesty property of D-002 at the smallest scale. Collapsing the two into one 'missing' rendering is the exact inference this scenario exists to refuse. Manual because it is a perceptual distinction across two encodings within one element rather than a presence check.

claims.statement: While any device is under a held lease, the holder and expiry are perceivable without opening that device.
claims.rationale: Priority 3 and D-006. Discovering a live session should never require navigation.

claims.statement: The kill control is operable from the keyboard whenever a session is live.
claims.rationale: A safety control that requires a pointer is not always available. SECURITY.md requires kill to be one action away from CLI or UI.

claims.statement: The count of unavailable capabilities reads before the device inventory; bookkeeping is never the first thing communicated.
claims.rationale: Absence is the page's product. Direction-aware so the order holds in RTL.

claims.statement: When the reach plane is unreachable, known devices remain listed alongside an assertive notice rather than disappearing.
claims.rationale: DVC-P0-003. A device that vanishes reads as 'not controlled'; the truth is 'controlled, currently unreachable, for this reason'.

claims.statement: The empty state renders guidance for attaching a device rather than a blank table.
claims.rationale: First-run is the most likely empty state, and the next action is not guessable — it involves pairing through another scenario.
